title: Exploring perceptual straightness in learned visual representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.34678v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humans have been shown to use a "straightened" encoding to represent the natural visual world as it evolves in time (H\'enaff et al. 2019). In the context of discrete video sequences, "straightened" means that changes between frames follow a more linear path in representation space at progressively deeper levels of processing. While deep convolutional networks are often proposed as models of human visual processing, many do not straighten natural videos. In this paper, we explore the relationship between network architecture, differing types of robustness, biologically-inspired filtering mechanisms, and representational straightness in response to time-varying input; we identify strengths and limitations of straightness as a useful way of evaluating neural network representations. We find that (1) adversarial training leads to straighter representations in both CNN and transformer-based architectures but (2) this effect is task-dependent

translated_title: 探索习得视觉表征中的感知直线性
translated_abstract: 人类已被证明使用一种“拉直”的编码方式来表征随时间演变的自然视觉世界（Hénaff et al. 2019）。在离散视频序列的背景下，“拉直”意味着在逐渐加深处理层次的过程中，帧与帧之间的变化在表示空间中遵循更加线性的路径。尽管深度卷积网络常被作为人类视觉处理的模型提出，但许多网络并不能“拉直”自然视频。在本文中，我们探索了网络架构、不同类型的鲁棒性、受生物学启发的过滤机制与表示直线性在响应时变输入时的关系；我们识别了直线性作为评估神经网络表示的一种有用方式的优势与局限。我们发现：（1）对抗训练在CNN和基于Transformer的架构中都能产生更直的表示，但（2）这种效果是依赖于任务的。
tldr: 本研究探讨了网络架构、鲁棒性与生物启发机制对视觉表征“直线性”的影响，发现对抗训练能使CNN和Transformer架构都产生更直的表征，但该效果依赖于具体任务。
en_tdlr: This study explores how network architecture, robustness types, and biologically-inspired mechanisms relate to representational straightness, finding that adversarial training yields straighter representations in both CNN and transformer architectures, though this effect is task-dependent.
